findings.reason: the builder cannot tell whether the intended observable is strict alternation (requiring a count-normalised tie-break the mechanism does not describe) or drain-first, and will pick one the done-when then contradicts.
findings.text: §3 ranks entries by "their session's use of the lane" and the recommended `priority-measure` is "runs in flight", but §3's done-when (line 62) asserts admissions "alternate in the lighter session's favour"; a session holding zero runs outranks a session holding many for all of the many, so the mechanism yields drain-the-lighter-queue-first, not alternation

findings.reason: without a declared bound the node writes whatever constant it guesses, and the assertion cannot fail on the unfixed code.
findings.text: §3's third bullet asserts "an entry that has waited past a stated bound is admitted ahead of a lighter session's newer entry" but no section states the bound, its units or its value, so the starvation guarantee cannot be tested

findings.reason: a build node following the note would dispatch §2/§3 with the decisions that fix their scope still open.
findings.text: the followup's ordering ("§2 and §3 can run together; §4 needs both and the `drainer` decision") omits that §2 is gated by the unresolved `lane-scope` decision, which selects whether this plan queues at all on the local lane vs every lane, and §3 by `priority-measure`; neither is named as a prerequisite
